commands.review_summary:
Updates the direct @types/node dependency and its lockfile resolution from 22.20.1 to 26.1.1.

Reproducibility: yes. from source inspection: the changed declaration package targets Node 26 while the manifest continues to support Node 22, so a Node 26-only API could pass typechecking without existing on the minimum runtime. The supplied context also shows verify failing, although its exact failure log was unavailable.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A mechanical repair can preserve the supported Node 22 contract by narrowing the dependency to the latest 22.x release and regenerating the lockfile.

target.title: fix(feishu): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a stalled Feishu (Lark SDK) inbound media download body blocks the channel's agent-reply workflow indefinitely because the underlying Node.js `Readable` async iterator never settles on empty/stalled streams. Additionally preserves the established Feishu timeout policy: the per-chunk idle timeout is derived from the canonical `resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs()` resolver (respecting `OPENCLAW_FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` env var, account config, and default) instead of a hardcoded 30s value.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap each `AsyncIterable.next()` call in `Promise.race` against a configurable timeout so stalled Lark SDK bodies cannot hang inbound dispatch.
- **Do NOT `await` iterator.return()** in the finally block — Node Readable async-iterator `return()` hangs when the underlying source is stalled (waits for a `readable` event that never fires). Instead, explicitly destroy the source on timeout so the underlying Readable (and its HTTP resource) close, then call `iterator.return()` without awaiting for safe measure.
- Thread the canonical Feishu timeout (`resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs`) from `saveMessageResourceFeishu()` through `saveMessageResourceWithType()` → `saveFeishuResponseMedia()` → `saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout()`, so the per-chunk idle deadline respects the user's configured HTTP timeout policy. A local `save` wrapper in `saveFeishuResponseMedia` keeps the call sites single-line and `media.ts` under its LOC baseline.
- Drop an unused `export` on `sanitizeFileNameForUpload` (internal helper, never imported outside `media.ts`).
- No new config/env surface. The timeout inherits the existing Feishu HTTP timeout policy.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "feishu chunk-idle timeout media download stall"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A stalled Lark SDK media stream (TCP accepted, headers received, body never produces chunks) would hang inbound dispatch indefinitely — no agent reply, no error logged.
- **After**: Stream times out after the resolved idle period with `FeishuInboundMediaTimeoutError`. The underlying source Readable is explicitly destroyed so the HTTP resource closes. Normal progressing streams are unaffected.

## Verification

- Exact head: `d39dd2a`
- `oxfmt --check extensions/feishu/src/media.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.proof.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts` — passed.
- `oxlint <same files>` — passed; exit 0.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.proof.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

- Full suite: `pnpm test extensions/feishu` — pending Testbox run.
- Mutation check: revert the `withChunkIdleTimeout` wrapper and the proof test fails (stalled Readable hangs forever with no timeout).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: chunk-idle timeout on stalled Feishu/Lark SDK media download stream, with canonical Feishu HTTP timeout policy preserved.
Real environment tested: Node 22, real production functions (saveMediaStream, withChunkIdleTimeout, resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs), real Node.js Readable streams (same boundary Lark SDK `getReadableStream()` returns).
Exact commands run:

```bash
node --import tsx proof-feishu-media-chunk-idle.mts
```

Observed output after fix:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=d39dd2ae9992d1cf8c06b3586ed924eb02396495

[case 1] negative control — stalled Node.js Readable without idle wrap
  ok: stalled Readable without idle wrap stays pending (>300ms)
  info: outcome=still-pending wait_ms=300 without_idle_wrap=true

[case 2] positive control — stalled Readable with idle wrap times out
  ok: saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout rejected on stalled Readable
  ok: error name is FeishuInboundMediaTimeoutError (got: FeishuInboundMediaTimeoutError)
  ok: chunkTimeoutMs matches input (got: 50)
  ok: timeout fires within 3s (elapsed_ms=66)
  ok: source Readable is destroyed after timeout
  info: elapsed_ms=66 timed_out=true chunkTimeoutMs=50 destroyed=true

[case 3] valid response — progressing Readable completes without timeout
  ok: saved media size matches input (expected=4, got=4)
  ok: contentType preserved (got: image/jpeg)
  info: size=4 contentType=image/jpeg timed_out=false

[case 4] valid response — multi-chunk Readable completes within deadline
  ok: multi-chunk total size correct (expected=1280, got=1280)
  info: chunks=3 total_bytes=1280 timed_out=false

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

Evidence:
- Real `saveMediaStream` called with chunk-idle wrapped Readable stream — through the exact production boundary
- Stalled Node.js Readable (same API Lark SDK returns) stays pending without wrap (case 1 proves unbounded wait)
- With idle wrap, same stalled Readable times out at ~66ms with `chunkTimeoutMs=50` AND the source is destroyed (case 2)
- Progressing Readable with 4-byte JPEG completes without timeout: `size=4 timed_out=false` (case 3)
- Multi-chunk Readable (3 chunks, 1280 bytes) completes: `chunks=3 total_bytes=1280 timed_out=false` (case 4)
- On timeout, the source Readable is explicitly destroyed (`destroyed=true`) so the underlying stream and HTTP resource close — confirmed by assertion (case 2)
- `iterator.return()` is NOT awaited in the finally block — the source is destroyed before reaching finally, so the underlying resource is released regardless
- Canonical timeout resolver (`resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs`) threads through the full call chain: `saveMessageResourceFeishu` → `saveMessageResourceWithType` → `saveFeishuResponseMedia` → `saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout`

What was not tested: Real Lark SDK media download against Feishu servers; real message dispatch through Feishu's cloud API. The fix operates on the Node.js Readable boundary where Lark SDK returns a stream — the proof tests that exact boundary with real Node.js Readable objects.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. The fix only wraps an existing AsyncIterable with a timeout raceguard. No new config surface, no environment variables, no behavior change for normally-progressing streams. The per-chunk idle timeout now derives from the canonical Feishu HTTP timeout resolver, so users with custom `OPENCLAW_FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` or account-level `httpTimeoutMs` retain their existing policy. The critical design decision (explicit source destroy on timeout, then non-awaited iterator.return()) is proven correct: Node Readable async-iterator return() hangs on stalled sources, but destroy forces the resource closed regardless. The 30s default (from `FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS`) matches Telegram's established download idle floor.
